alternatives.argument: The local proof covers every proper nonzero subspace by an open set of based loops that fail to preserve it. Compactness of the finite Grassmannian union extracts finitely many loops; the positive continuous failure function has a positive minimum; the linear-ODE comparison estimate preserves that minimum under small C1 perturbations. The current lemma defines irreducibility by invariant subspaces of based holonomy and proves finite witnesses and openness only; no stabilizer/properness claim is used.

The local proof applies relative avoidance to a point for nonemptiness, to an affine interval relative to its endpoints for path connectedness, and to the affine cone over each based sphere map relative to the boundary. Contracting the repaired disk to its boundary basepoint gives the based nullhomotopy.

sources.title: Dominic Walpuski, Differential Geometry III: Gauge Theory (full lecture notes)
sources.locator: §5.13.2–§5.13.3, PDF pp. 113–116, through Remark 5.76: Sobolev connections, gauge action, properness context, stabilizer centralizer, irreducibility convention, and the holonomy caveat.

contents.name: Definition 5.71, Sobolev connections and gauge transformations

source_review.read_extent: The complete Definition 5.71 and its consequences on PDF pp. 113–114 were inspected.
source_review.supports: The notes define Sobolev connection and gauge spaces, their affine model, right gauge action, and smoothness under the stated regularity condition.
source_review.limitations: The notes use W^{k+1,p} connections and W^{k+2,p} gauges; matching H^q/H^{q+1} requires p=2 and an index shift. This setup does not prove the finite holonomy witness.

contents.name: Proposition 5.72, properness of the Sobolev gauge action
contents.reason: Properness of the full Sobolev gauge action is outside the finite holonomy and weak topology claims proved in this assigned pair; no properness theorem is asserted here.

contents.name: Definition 5.73, isotropy group of a connection

source_review.read_extent: Definition 5.73 on PDF p. 115 was inspected together with Proposition 5.74.
source_review.supports: It identifies the isotropy group as the gauge transformations preserving the connection, the stabilizer notion used by the conditional batch-56 supplier.
source_review.limitations: The local finite-loop witness argument does not use a Banach quotient or the slice theorem.

contents.name: Proposition 5.74, stabilizer evaluation and the holonomy centralizer

source_review.read_extent: The complete statement and proof of Proposition 5.74 on PDF p. 115 were inspected.
source_review.supports: Evaluation at a fiber identifies the stabilizer with the centralizer of the based holonomy group; the proof uses parallel transport in both directions.
source_review.limitations: This is a Sobolev stabilizer statement. The current batch-56 carrier and its ready Step 1 record were separately inspected; independent proof acceptance is outside this source disposition.

source_review.read_extent: Definition 5.75 on PDF p. 115 was inspected.
source_review.supports: The notes define irreducibility by the evaluated stabilizer being the center of the compact structure group.
source_review.limitations: The local statement uses invariant subspaces of the standard SU(N) representation; equivalence follows from the separately proved unitary Schur argument, not by identifying holonomy with all of SU(N).

contents.name: Remark 5.76, holonomy can be proper with centralizer equal to the center

source_review.read_extent: Remark 5.76 on PDF p. 115 was inspected.
source_review.supports: The notes explicitly warn that irreducibility does not require the holonomy group to equal the full structure group.
source_review.limitations: The finite-loop and openness proof is supplied locally.
